latest_release.name: Termix v26.11.1
latest_release.body:
> [!TIP]
> Termix is free and always will be. If it's useful to you, consider [donating](https://donate.termix.site/donate/) to support development.

### Added

- Plugins in the desktop app can drag files out to Explorer or Finder
- Termix actions: plugins can declare what they do once, and it works from the API with permission checks, dry runs, run history and approvals
- API keys can be limited to reading or running actions, when an admin makes them
- A click on a host can open its host page, when a plugin offers one
- Plugins can build pages of tiles you drag and resize, and add many copies of one dashboard card, each with its own settings
- A plugin a newer release ships is downloaded on its own when your image does not have it, and tried again on the next start when offline
- Plugins can decide who may connect to a host, so a host can need approved access before an SSH or remote desktop session opens
- When more than one plugin flags a host, its row shows one status dot with every reason in its tooltip
- Plugins that issue SSH certificates can save them on the SSH key login they were issued for
- Cmd+B shows or hides the sidebar, and can be changed in keybindings
- The macOS menu bar icon can be monochrome (the default), in color or hidden, from the Termix menu
- Browser back and forward, and the mouse back and forward buttons, move between the tabs you used instead of leaving Termix
- Closing a tab goes back to the tab you used before it
- Admin setting to stop anyone saving passwords and keys on hosts and credentials. Termix asks for them when connecting (#1753)
- A signed in user can prove a second factor again, for plugins that ask before something sensitive
- Desktop app: a credential can be kept on this device only, and used as a personal login for a shared host or folder. It is never sent to the server (#1749)

### Changed

- Inputs, selects, tab groups and menus share one fill and one border color
- Plugin cards and pages use the dashboard look everywhere, with shared lines between sections instead of separate boxes with gaps
- The Plugins tab and plugin pages use the same look
- List rows in plugins follow the host list status colors: accent for good, dark for offline or bad
- Line charts that cover a few minutes show seconds in their times
- Plugins a new release adds to the image start on only when they are recommended. The rest are installed and left off for an admin to turn on
- Session tokens are stored as hashes, so a database copy holds no working logins (#1753)

- Host status, import and export, and credential tools now start on for new installs
- Sync now starts on in a new desktop app, so it can link to a server
- The first run plugin picker leaves plugins you did not choose off instead of removing them
- The Linux Flatpak now installs from flatpak.termix.site on x86_64 and arm64, and `flatpak update` keeps it current
- Dropdowns and text areas are the same size as the text fields next to them
- A page's own tabs sit above its search bar
- A plugin view that is still starting shows the same loading spinner as the rest of Termix

### Fixed

- Exporting hosts keeps each host status check setting and interval (#1787)
- A linked desktop app now updates a plugin that came with the app when the server has a newer copy (#1785)
- The first run plugin picker no longer sets the default layout and themes to Remove. They always stay on
- Alerts with no icon no longer squeeze their text to one word per line
- Password fields with the show button are the same height as the other fields next to them
- Button groups next to tabs no longer touch the lines of the tab row
- The Secure your account setup step no longer shows up empty when no passkey or authenticator plugin is on
- An installed plugin update older than the copy in a newer image is removed at startup instead of logging an error every boot
- Canceling a download to the desktop app right as it starts no longer leaves a partial file behind
- Changing two interf

detail.readme:
Termix

Self-hosted, plugin-based server management


## Overview Termix is a free, open source, self-hosted server management platform built on plugins. The core keeps your hosts, credentials, users, sharing and sessions. Everything else, like the SSH terminal, remote desktop, file manager, Docker and metrics, is a plugin you can turn on, off or remove. It runs on web, desktop and mobile. Think of it as a free, self-hosted Termius.
## Try the Demo Try it at [demo.termix.site](https://demo.termix.site/). Any username and password works.
## Core What every install has, with or without plugins: - Hosts: Save hosts in nested folders with tags and parent hosts, bulk edit, import and export, and use Quick Connect for one-off connections - Credentials: Reuse saved passwords and keys across hosts, with host defaults you can set for the server, a user or a folder - Sharing and Roles: Share hosts, credentials and folders with users or roles at four levels: connect, view, edit and manage - Accounts: Local accounts, sessions you can see and revoke, trusted devices, API keys and an audit log - Security: Passwords, keys and other secrets are encrypted per user, and the database can be encrypted on disk - Desktop Sync: The desktop app runs on its own and can link to a Termix server to keep an offline copy of your account - Interface: Tabs and split screen, a command palette (double tap left shift), rebindable shortcuts, themes, branding and around 30 languages - Databases: SQLite by default, with PostgreSQL and MySQL supported too
## Plugins Plugins add everything else. Admins can install, update or remove plugins from the Plugins tab, and each plugin has its own repo. These ship in the default image: | Plugin | What it does | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | [Alerts](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Plugin-Alerts) | and Podman containers on your hosts over SSH, with logs, stats and a console. | | [File Manager](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Plugin-File-Manager) | Browse, edit and move files over SFTP, including All other official plugins (54) These ship in the `-full` image tags (like `latest-full`) and the full desktop builds. Want to build your own? Start from the [plugin template](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix-Plugin-Template). Plugins you can install are listed in the [registry](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix-Registry). Turn on the community registry in Plugins, Registries to install plugins made by other people, or add your own registry. See [submitting a plugin](https://docs.termix.site/develop/community-registry) and [hosting your own registry](https://docs.termix.site/develop/registries#host-your-own-registry).
## Platform Support
Platform Distribution
Web Any modern browser (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) | PWA support
Windows x64/ia32 Portable | EXE and MSI Installer | Full EXE (all plugins) | Chocolatey
Linux x64/arm64/armv7l Portable | AUR | AppImage | Deb | Full AppImage and Deb (all plugins) | Flatpak
macOS Universal/x64/arm64, v12.0+ Apple App Store | DMG | Full DMG (all plugins) | Homebrew
iOS/iPadOS v15.1+ Apple App Store | IPA
Android v7.0+ Google Play Store | APK

## Installation See the [docs](https://docs.termix.site/install) for install steps on every platform. On macOS, Termix, Menu Bar Icon picks a monochrome icon (the default), a color icon or no icon. The choice is saved on this device. With the icon hidden, open Termix from the Dock to change it back, and closing the last window quits the app. Sample Docker Compose file. Remote desktop (RDP, VNC and Telnet) is built in, so nothing else needs to run next to it: ```yaml services: termix: image: ghcr.io/termix-ssh/termix:latest container_name: termix restart: unless-stopped ports: - "8080:8080" volumes: - termix-data:/app/data environment: PORT: "8080" volumes: termix-data: driver: local ``` ### Cloud Hosting If Termix runs on the network it manages, an outage takes it down right when you need it. A VPS keeps it reachable, gives you a static IP and works from anywhere without a VPN or port forward. [GINERNET](https://docs.termix.site/install/ginernet) sponsors Termix and the docs have a setup guide for their VPS.
## Donate Termix has no paid plans. Donations cover servers, domains and development time. [Donate](https://donate.termix.site/)
## Sponsors For a paid sponsor spot, email [mail@termix.site](mailto:mail@termix.site).

                           

## Support Bugs and ideas for Termix itself (login, hosts, credentials, sharing, sync, the app and desktop app) go in this repo: [report a bug](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) or [request a feature](https://github.com/Termix-SSH/Termix/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml). Every plugin has its own repo, so a problem with the terminal, file manager, Docker, remote desktop or any other plugin goes in that plugin's repo (see the table above, or use Report an issue on the plugin's page in the app, which fills in your versions for you). Not sure where it goes? Open it here and it will be moved. You need a GitHub account. Add as much detail as you can, in English if possible. For discussions and questions, join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/jVQGdvHDrf) server. Update videos are on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@TermixSSH/videos).
